title: Unified Inference 7 Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Q1 2026)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Redwood Inference's Unified Inference product line as of Q1 2026. It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market and customer-facing teams.

Goals and success metrics:

- Goal 1: Provide a unified API and operational model that lets customers run LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with minimal changes to application code.
- Goal 2: Reduce per-token inference cost for target enterprise workloads by 30% vs baseline (2024) through autoscaling, intelligent batching, and quantization recommendations.
- Goal 3: Achieve 99.9% availability for Dedicated customers under contract and maintain 95th-percentile request latency SLOs per model tier.

Key success metrics (KPIs):

1. Adoption: number of customers using Dedicated or Private deployments (target 20 by EOY 2026).
2. Cost reduction: average per-token cost delta reported by customers after adopting Redwood Optimize suggestions (target -30%).
3. Reliability: platform-wide availability for paid tiers >= 99.9%.
4. Latency: 95th percentile tail latency for small-generation workloads < 300ms for low-latency model tier.

1) Product Requirements (PRD / Scope)

Overview:
- Unified Inference must present a single REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across deployment modes. Customers can pin model versions and rollout policies independent of infra.

Core functional requirements (MUST):
- R1: API parity across Hosted, Dedicated and Private for generation and embeddings (endpoints, parameters, streaming).
- R2: Model catalog with metadata (architecture, quantization profile, token cost estimate, latency profile per region).
- R3: Rollout & routing policies: canary, A/B, and automatic fallbacks to variant models when capacity constrained.
- R4: Observability: per-route token-level cost breakdown, latency distributions, error rate, and per-model quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
- R5: Cost optimization toolkit: automated batching suggestions, prefix/KV caching toggles, and quantization recommendations per workload.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- NFR1: 95th percentile latency SLOs published per model tier.
- NFR2: Configurable autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools (min/max nodes, burst capacity).
- NFR3: Data residency controls for Private deployments (region selection, retention policy).

Out-of-scope for Q1 2026:
- Deep integration with third-party feature stores for prompt caching (planned Q3 2026).

Ownership and stakeholders:

- Tech lead: Michael Chen (eng-serving-runtime)

- Sales/Evangelism: Priya Nair (go-to-market)

2) Design Specifications (high-level)

Architecture summary:
- Front door: API Gateway with request metadata tagging (customer_id, route, model_variant).
- Router: Smart routing service implements policies (latency, cost, region, customer-tier) and falls back to compatible model variants.
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized inference nodes with quantization kernels. Supports continuous batching and KV/prefix cache.
- Control plane: Model catalog, rollout manager, observability ingest, and Optimize recommendations service.

Design notes and decisions:
- Decision DR-2025-07: Use model-variant compatibility graph for safe automatic fallback (stores tensor layout & numeric precision compatibility flags).
- Decision DR-2025-11: Prefer in-memory prefix cache on Dedicated pools to reduce cross-instance KV fetches; fallback is shared Redis for Private deployments with large clusters.

APIs and payload examples:
- Generation endpoint example (pseudocode):
  POST /v1/generate {"model":"redwood-unified-4.1","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":256,"top_p":0.95}
- Streaming: chunked SSE or HTTP/2 streams with 'delta' messages.

Observability contract:
- Emit per-request spans with these tags: customer_id, route_id, model_variant, node_id, batch_size, cache_hit (true/false), latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_code.
- Dashboard requirements: per-model P95/P99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate by route, recent regressions from eval harness.

SLOs and thresholds (example):
- Dedicated (premium): availability >= 99.9% monthly; P95 generation latency <= 300ms for small-gen (<=128 tokens).
- Hosted (standard): availability >= 99.5%; P95 generation latency <= 600ms.

3) Roadmap & Themes (next 12 months)

Quarterly themes (high level):
- Q2 2026: Stabilize Dedicated autoscaling + Rollouts (canaries, A/B), GA of per-route billing analytics.
- Q3 2026: Improve Optimize \u2014 workload-aware quantization profiles + recommendation engine; Private deployment on-prem packaging improvements.
- Q4 2026: Model catalog expansion (community-sourced validated variants), global region expansion (APAC), compliance packages for regulated industries.

Planned milestones and owners:
1. Dedicated autoscaling GA (Owner: eng-sre) \u2014 target: 2026-05-15 \u2014 success: autoscaling tests + 3 pilot customers onboarded.
2. Rollouts v1 (Owner: eng-platform) \u2014 target: 2026-06-30 \u2014 success: feature flag controlled canary deploys with automatic rollback on error budget breach.
3. Redwood Optimize v3 (Owner: applied-ml-and-evals) \u2014 target: 2026-09-01 \u2014 success: -25% cost on top-10 customer workloads in pilot.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency on kernel optimizations from eng-serving-runtime for new quantization profiles.
- Risk: model quality regression when recommending aggressive quantization; mitigated via eval harness and automatic rollback on quality regression alerts.

4) Pricing & Packaging Guidance

Pricing pillars:
- Usage-first for Hosted (per-token generation + per-embedding unit).
- Committed monthly/annual billing for Dedicated (base platform + node-hour consumption + burst buffer pricing).
- Private: licensing + deployment fee + optional support SLAs.

Reference pricing bands (internal guidance):
- Hosted standard: $0.0008 per token (generation) for base models; $0.0016 per token for high-performance variants. Embeddings: $0.0005 per vector.
- Dedicated (committed): platform fee $2,000 / month + $X per reserved GPU-hour (tiered by GPU type). Example packages for mid-market: 4x A100-equivalent reserved = $Y/month (negotiated).
- Private: one-time deployment license + annual support (TBD per contract).

Discounting & packaging rules:
- Offer usage credits for migration pilots (up to $25k) and migration assistance for Dedicated commitments.
- Channel/partner discounts to be approved by Sales Ops for marketplace listings.

Billing & metering notes:
- Meter at the route level with token counts and model_variant tags. Support re-billing for failed requests where customer supplied invalid input.

5) Release Notes (most recent release: 2026-02-10)

Release v2026.02.10 \u2014 Unified Inference platform
- GA: per-route billing analytics and token-level cost dashboards.
- New: Rollout manager alpha \u2014 supports canary and A/B deploys for Hosted and Dedicated.
- Improvement: Serving runtime updated kernel selection reduces median generation latency by 12% for Llama2-family variants.
- Fixes: Resolved a cache invalidation bug that could cause stale KV lookups during rolling upgrades.

Rollout plan for latest release:
1. Canary: enable rollout manager for 10% of Hosted traffic and gather metrics for 7 days.
2. Pilot: onboard 3 Dedicated beta customers for autoscaling rules.
3. GA: rollout to all Hosted customers and opt-in for Dedicated within 6 weeks.

Operational runbook highlights (for SREs and support):
- If P95 latency > target by 50%: 1) route traffic away from overloaded pool (smart-router), 2) disable batching temporarily, 3) escalate to eng-serving-runtime on-call.
- If regression alert for eval prompt-set fires: 1) pause rollout, 2) create a triage ticket and run eval-harness locally, 3) fallback to previous model_variant until regression cleared.
